GUIDED TUTORIAL

Audit a Supplemental ICT/SMC Term

Research non-standard terminology without elevating community labels into canonical ICT rules.

TUTORIAL MATERIALS
  • The existing source note and references for a selected concept
  • At least two source descriptions when available
  • A rule-definition sheet

Track prerequisites: entry-models-execution, futures-contract-roll-risk

01

WORKFLOW

Follow the practice sequence

  1. Step 1

    Start with the concept's evidence label and source note. Identify whether it is source-derived, supplemental, secondary or community terminology.

  2. Step 2

    Open each cited source and record its author, date, wording and exact boundary/trigger definition. Do not treat search results as official lesson verification.

  3. Step 3

    Compare definitions and list any disagreement. If no primary definition is available, retain the item as a research glossary note.

  4. Step 4

    Write a measurable operational version with timeframe, price boundary, close/wick condition and invalidation—or mark it as not yet operational.

  5. Step 5

    Only after the definition is stable should you collect examples for replay. Keep versions separate when source rules differ.

02

DELIVERABLE

What to create

A source-comparison note with at least two reference entries where available, rule variants, uncertainty statement and a not-to-trade-until-defined decision.
